ff_0328_3_verdict.label: legitimate — sanction via the established auto-additive channel; fix-iteration, not blocking
reasoning: ADR T-0328 §4.2 title states the process-start.ts freeze is 'contract-frozen, not byte-frozen' — its enforced invariant is the REST shape across the B/C/E seam (ADR T-0278 §2.2), checked by ci/checks/start-route-isolation.sh (static boundary: engine reached ONLY via injected FlowableClient, no own transport, no process.env reads, display-plane pg-free). I ran start-route-isolation.sh against this diff: PASS on all three arms (FF-7-1/7-2/7-3).

The ADR's own §5 (formal fitness-function enumeration, from which the http-route-auth-coverage.sh script was generated) states FF-0328-3 more strongly: 'secret-handle.ts and the process-start.ts body are not edited by the implementation' with ci_check literally 'git diff --quiet <merge-base> ... returns clean'. This is a genuine internal tension in the ADR: §4.2's narrative says 'contract, not bytes' while §5's formal spec (and the shipped script) encodes a strict byte-diff with zero carve-out for additive in-body edits. The script as written does not implement a contract-check for this file — it implements exactly the byte check §5 describes. So the coder's plain reading of the CHECK is correct (it is byte-strict); their reading of the ADR's INTENT (§4.2) is also correct (byte-freeze was never the actual security invariant — the façade-based G1 fix at the registration site was the intended closure path, and it doesn't require touching process-start.ts's body at all).

Ran http-route-auth-coverage.sh directly: FF-0328-1 (every route auth-covered) PASS, FF-0328-2 (no bare x-dev-user trust) PASS — the two REAL security invariants this check exists to enforce are both clean. Only FF-0328-3's literal byte-diff arm fails, and only against process-start.ts (secret-handle.ts is untouched, byte-identical).

Inspected the actual diff in src/http/process-start.ts and its records.ts sibling call site: the change adds a getActiveUserTasks(instanceId) read (already using the injected flowable client, no new transport) and threads approverRole/step/taskName into the pre-existing, already-optional appendProcessStarted(...) parameters. This is squarely inside the surface T-0575's OWN ADR (runtime_target list) and spec (§2, §6 exact-line table) names as one of the two required call sites for BUG-015 — there is no way to satisfy this task's contract without touching this file's body. The 201 response SHAPE (T-0328's real concern per §4.2) is unchanged: no new/removed/retyped response fields, no new request fields, no auth/identity logic touched.

Checked ci/checks/data/frozen-sanctions.jsonl for precedent specifically on http-route-auth-coverage.sh: zero prior entries. The 073-118 precedent chain the orchestrator's mandate references is entirely for ci/checks/dual-control-isolation.sh / defer-no-new-table.sh (migration ADD-COLUMN relief, a different check and a different class of invariant — additive schema changes vs. byte-diff route files). There is no existing auto_additive precedent for widening/narrowing FF-0328-3's FROZEN_FILES array or for granting a byte-diff exemption on a specific commit. This is a genuinely NEW class of sanction, not a mechanical repeat of an established pattern.

Despite being a new class, the sanction is still auto-additive-eligible on the same A-1..A-4 discipline the existing precedents use: (A-1) the exemption is additive to the check (either a FROZEN_FILES scope note or a merge-base pin, not a deletion of the byte-diff arm entirely) (A-2) it is scoped to exactly this task's diff, verified line-by-line above to touch only the BUG-015 call-site body, nothing else (A-3) the check's OTHER two arms (FF-0328-1, FF-0328-2 — the actual auth-bypass invariants) are independently verified green, unaffected (A-4) the ADR's own §4.2 text is the authorization source — this is not the coder inventing a new authority, it is resolving a documented internal contradiction between the ADR's narrative section and its formal fitness-function section in favor of the narrative section's explicitly stated intent, which is the SAME resolution direction ADR T-0328 itself used for secret-handle.ts's façade (additive fix, no founder thaw, because the frozen invariant is behavioral/contractual, not textual).

The coder did the right procedural thing: did not silently bypass, did not self-grant sanction, flagged the exact tension in notes_for_reviewer with both options spelled out. That is the honest-red posture this review process exists to catch and rule on.
ff_0328_3_verdict.recommended_followup: T-0576 (or a narrow fix-iteration on this task) should EITHER (1) narrow http-route-auth-coverage.sh's FF-0328-3 FROZEN_FILES array to secret-handle.ts only, updating the script's header comment and ADR-T0328 §5 point 3's wording to match §4.2's 'contract-frozen, not byte-frozen' framing for process-start.ts, backed by start-route-isolation.sh as the actual enforced contract; OR (2) add a durable frozen-sanctions.jsonl entry recording this exact commit-range exemption so the next task touching process-start.ts under the same BUG-015-class contract does not have to re-litigate this from scratch. Option 1 is preferable — it resolves the ADR's internal §4.2 vs §5 contradiction permanently instead of accumulating per-task sanction rows for a file that legitimately gets touched by every sibling task in its class (T-0439/T-0443/T-0483/T-0558 already did so post-freeze without any sanction row existing, per the coder's own git-log research in notes_for_reviewer).

findings.location: src/http/process-projection.ts resolveDefaultApproverRole / resolveDefaultApproveStep / resolveDefaultApproveTaskName; src/db/step-applier.ts resolveDefaultStepResultSlug; src/http/form-record-persister.ts resolveTelApplicationSlug/resolveApprovalFormRegistrySlug
findings.issue: Config-primitive env values (CHOROS_DEFAULT_APPROVER_ROLE, CHOROS_DEFAULT_STEP_RESULT_SLUG, CHOROS_TEL_APPLICATION_SLUG, CHOROS_DEFAULT_APPROVE_STEP/TASK_NAME) are read as raw strings with only an empty/whitespace check (`v.trim() !== ""`), no format/slug validation. This does not open an injection path — every one of these values flows into the SAME parameterized-query / audit-payload-string slots that today's hardcoded literals already occupy (no string concatenation into SQL, no eval, no path traversal), so the security posture is unchanged from today's hardcoded behavior. It is purely an operator-trust boundary: a misconfigured env var (e.g. containing whitespace-only-looking unicode, or an unintended slug) would silently become the new 'default' with no startup-time validation/logging of the resolved value.
findings.suggestion: Optional hardening for a future task: log the resolved config-primitive values once at server startup (or validate against a slug-shape regex) so a misconfigured env var is visible in ops rather than silently changing default routing behavior. Not blocking — matches the trust level of every other process.env-sourced config primitive already in the codebase.

findings.issue: The per-task identitylinks fetch is a genuine N+1 (one extra HTTP round-trip per active task returned by the instance-scoped LIST query), but it is correctly BOUNDED: the outer query is `?processInstanceId={id}` (one instance's active tasks only, never a tenant-wide or cross-instance scan), and a single instance realistically has O(1) concurrent active user-tasks (one, or a handful on an AND-split). A failed identitylinks fetch for one task degrades that task's candidateGroups to [] (caught internally, never propagates), so the caller's resolveDefaultApproverRole() fallback applies per-task, not for the whole call. Confirmed by reading the diff and by SA/db-test structure — no fan-out beyond one instance's active-task set.
findings.suggestion: None required. Documented correctly in the coder's own comment; flagging only so the bound is explicit in the review record as the mandate requested.
